Point No.1 and 2 : The learned counsel for the accused Sri.C R submits the ingredients of alleged offence are not made out.
In fact the place is not a public place, it is the office of the accused as per the allegations of complaint.
Therefore the question of ingredients of offence punishable u/s.3(1)(r) of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989 or even 3(1)(s) are not made out.

With regard to the offence punishable u/s.420 of IPC, there is no any entrustment made,
parting of any property with inducement or deceived by the accused so as to part with the alledged money.
In this case allegations is Rs.1,30,00,000/- has been given financial lending for the purpose of business in December 2016 by promising the same to be returned within 1 month.
However there is no any document being executed with regard to payment of such huge amount of Rs.1,30,00,000/-.
The complainant has not produced any documents to show she had such a huge amount with her and there is no documents placed to show handing over of such amount of Rs.1,30,00,000/-.
The question that there is no repayment made by the complainant, herself has further mentioned cheques have been given.
However the cheques are not placed in the case on hand so as to consider whether the intention of the accused is to deceive by issuing cheques.
Admittedly the cheques have been placed for recovery before court in Negotiable instruments case is the admission of the complainant.
In fact as on 26.11.2018 when the complainant went to the office of accused in fact there is CCTV footages available.
Thus footages have not been placed by the Investigating Officer so as to show that accused was approached by the complainant.
In the case on hand, admittedly complainant has collected cheques for a tune of Rs.73 lakhs but not for Rs.1,30,00,000/- as complained.

Therefore when there is no match to the amount claimed to be refunded and the cheque collected, these facts create doubt with regard to whether any financial transaction did took place between accused and complainant.
9. The learned counsel for the accused argues complainant is not a layman when she is having business and transacting crores of rupees she had all the knowledge.
The complainant is a well educated person.
There is no any income tax returns or documents to show the source of income or in what manner complainant got the amount of Rs.1,30,00,000/- is placed on record.
Therefore the question of ingredients of offence punishable u/s.420 of IPC being committed, no any documents collected by the Investigating Officer nor placed.

In the evidence of P.W.4, specific admission have been got elicited wherein P.W.4 specifically deposes that he was also present at the time of demanding the amount from the accused, but the answers in the cross examination and even photographs were taken in the camera of the Investigating Officer.

In the cross examination of the P.W.1, the complainant never approached the place at the first instance even though she has collected cheque but as a counter to the complaint given by the accused she has filed this false complaint by invoking the provisions of SC/ST (POA) Act 1989.
Therefore the allegations made in the complaint by the complainant are not substantiated.
Hence the alleged ingredients of offence are not being made out.
